predictions.reasoning: A shift in the implied probability of Kamala Harris winning the 2028 Democratic nomination — an event more than three years away with no policy or governing consequence in the near term — carries essentially no information that liquid US markets would reprice within a 12-hour window. Primary-nomination odds this far out are dominated by name recognition and speculative churn, not fundamentals. There is no plausible transmission channel to broad equity levels, sectors, or FX on this horizon.

evidence_used: Market resolves on 2028 Democratic nomination, an event >3 years out
Nomination outcome has no near-term governing or policy effect
No sector or macro variable is directly tied to a single candidate's primary odds at this horizon
uncertainty_notes: A candidate primary market this far out is heavily noise-driven and illiquid
Even a large probability swing would not map to a fundamental asset repricing
Only an accompanying real-world headline (not the market move itself) could move assets

llm_justification.summary: This market concerns the 2028 Democratic presidential nomination for Kamala Harris — an event years away with no near-term economic or policy transmission channel. A move in its implied probability has no reliable, tradable implication for liquid public markets over a 12-hour horizon. The most honest mapping is 'unclear' with very low confidence and no tradable signal (well below the 700 bps threshold).
key_assumptions: Nomination odds this far out do not encode actionable near-term macro/policy information
No simultaneous market-moving real-world event is assumed
Broad ETFs are the only remotely relevant proxies, and even they are effectively unexposed
failure_modes: A sharp probability move could coincide with a genuine breaking headline (health event, scandal, resignation) that itself moves assets — but then the driver is the news, not this market
The proxy (SPY) is essentially unexposed to a single candidate's 2028 primary odds, making any inferred signal spurious
Thin prediction-market liquidity makes any 'move' likely a data artifact rather than information
